title: XLSM parse spike and PRD exit-figure reconciliation
parse_approach: spikes/spike_xlsm_parse.py runs two openpyxl 3.1.5 loads of v5.5_40L_Project_Tracker.xlsm: data_only=True for cached values and data_only=False for formulas. It enumerates sheet names; on Monthly Returns it detects bond columns by header keyword (Company Name/ISN/Status/Tenure/Interest Starting Month, fallback col A/B), counts bond rows from row 2, collects names/ISINs/tenure/start-month/status; it scans row 1 from column N rightward (to col 300) parsing date and mmm-yy headers into YYYY-MM; it sums money columns G (Principle TL Amount), K (Till Rerun Amount), L (Balance Amount) over bond rows with None and non-numeric accounting; it runs a per-sheet formula-vs-static census on the formula workbook and probes whether Dashboard COUNTA/COUNTIF/SUM cells have cached values. Output is one JSON object on stdout; exit 0 on success, 1 on fatal error with errors listed in the JSON.

formula_static_findings.home_plan: Mixed as expected: 184 formula / 444 static cells. Formulas sit in derived columns E (88, per-year interest =Cn*Dn) and G (88, =(En/12)*Fn) plus a few in B, C, I, J (1/1/3/3); date, month index, saving, rate, countdown and the trailing Per Month / Per Year / TL summary rows are static. data_only=True returns cached values for every formula cell, so a no-formula-engine importer can read them.
formula_static_findings.monthly_returns_money_columns: All 30 formulas are K2:K16 (=SUM(Nn:XFDn) over the month grid) and L2:L16 (=Kn-Jn); column G (investment) is static. Cached values exist for all of them (none_cells = 0 across G/K/L for the 15 bond rows).
formula_static_findings.dashboard: 8 formulas (4 COUNTA/COUNTIF in column B, 4 SUM in column E); all 8 have cached values (dashboard_cached = true). Cached SUMs match the spike's own column sums exactly: E3=550000.00, E4=28500.00, E5=-521500.00.
formula_static_findings.bond_watch_list: 128 formulas across analytics columns I, L, N-U (discount/TDS/yield style calcs) over 197 static cells; out of MVP scope (FR-11) but parseable the same way.

import_design_risks: SUM K actual 28500.00 vs PRD/SRS exit figure 28500.00 (delta 7500.00). The month grid itself (cols 14..96, rows 2..16) sums to exactly 28500.00, and a full-workbook numeric scan found no cell within 0.02 of 28500.00 (or -521500.00) on any sheet. The PRD exit figures are not present in this workbook snapshot - snapshot drift or an undocumented derivation. Import parity tests (FR-09, NFR-10, SM-01) must be re-baselined against the workbook, which the PRD itself declares the source of truth.

SUM L actual -521500.00 vs PRD/SRS exit figure -521500.00 (delta -100000.00). Workbook L = K - J (maturity amount); SUM J = 570000.00, so 28500.00 - 570000.00 = -521500.00. The PRD pair is internally consistent only under Balance = Till Return - Total Investment: 28500.00 - 550000.00 = -521500.00 exactly. There is a definition conflict between the PRD exit math (subtracts investment) and the workbook formula (subtracts maturity amount); the target definition must be settled before import parity can pass.

K and L are formulas, not stored numbers. An importer with no formula engine must recompute K as the sum of the month-grid row and L as K - J; reading K/L as static or trusting any pre-baked value risks silent wrongness. Dashboard caches currently agree with data_only sums, but caches reflect the same drifted snapshot.
Sheet name is 'Bond - Watch list ' with a trailing space; sheet lookup must trim/normalize rather than match exact strings.

Bond names live in column E (Company Name); col A is Status and col B is Purchase Date. Column-by-header detection (or at least E, not A/B) is required - aligns with FR-23 (no position/header coupling).

Month grid is 83 headers 2025-09..2032-07 in row 1 cols 14..96, then 4 empty header cells before the sheet dimension ends (col 100). The spike brief's ~96-month assumption is wrong; 83 matches the PRD's own '83-month history' (US-05) and DATA-02 ('Sep-2025..Jul-2032+'). Grid extent must be derived from headers at runtime, never hardcoded (FR-18/NFR-9).
Home Plan formula/static mix (184/444) confirms ERR-06: import must preserve static inputs verbatim and take cached (or recomputed) values for derived cells.
Dashboard caches exist for all COUNTA/COUNTIF/SUM cells, so a naive importer could trust them - but NFR-7 requires live recompute anyway; treat caches as parse evidence only, not as truth.

oletools was not needed for cell-level import (openpyxl alone parsed every sheet). Extracting VBA behavior (status engine, open/save dashboard rebuild, MsgBox quirks) is separate, unproven work outside this spike.

g1.question: openpyxl/oletools parse path viable for one-time import?
g1.evidence: spikes/spike_xlsm_parse.py exits 0 with errors=[] and one JSON object: all 5 sheets enumerated ('Note', 'Bond - Watch list ' (trailing space), 'Monthly Returns', 'Dashboard', 'Home Plan'); both data_only passes succeed; Monthly Returns yields 15 bond rows (E2:E16) with 15 ISIN-like ids, tenure/start/status columns, month headers first=2025-09 last=2032-07 count=83; sums G=550000.00, K=28500.00, L=-521500.00 with none_cells=0; per-sheet formula census complete (Home Plan 184 formula/444 static as predicted); Dashboard COUNTA/COUNTIF/SUM cells: 8/8 cached values readable. Cell-level one-time import is viable on openpyxl alone (oletools only relevant for VBA extraction, not exercised here). The two reconciliation mismatches are data/definition issues in the PRD exit figures, not parse failures.
